title: Synthesis and Structural Characterization of Nonanuclear Lanthanide Complexes

material_class.structural_family: nonanuclear oxo-hydroxo β-diketonate cluster with two vertex-sharing square-pyramidal [Ln5(μ4-O)(μ3-OH)4]9+ units

synthesis.procedure: LnCl3·6H2O (Ln = Sm; 1.00 mmol) and benzoylacetone (HBA, 1.78 mmol) were dissolved in ca. 15 mL of methanol. Triethylamine (3.75 mmol) was added dropwise and the mixture was stirred at room temperature for 24 h. Light yellow precipitate was collected by filtration, washed with methanol, and dried in vacuum (yield ca. 70%). The product was dissolved in CHCl3/CH3OH (1:10 v/v), filtered, and the filtrate was allowed to stand at room temperature; cubic crystals suitable for X-ray analysis were harvested after 10 days. The synthesis is the shared procedure for 1–5 (Ln:HBA = 9:16) by partial hydrolysis of trace water in methanol in air.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution synthesis in air followed by recrystallization from CHCl3/CH3OH (1:10 v/v)
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: precipitate filtered, washed with methanol, dried in vacuum; dissolved in CHCl3/CH3OH (1:10), filtered; cubic crystals from standing filtrate at room temperature after 10 days

properties.summary: Variable-temperature magnetization of 1–5 was measured at 2–300 K. For 1, μeff decreases continuously on cooling, indicating mainly single-ion Sm3+ behavior rather than strong interion coupling.

measurements.name: variable-temperature magnetization
measurements.conditions: 2–300 K; Oxford MagLab 2000; diamagnetic corrections from Pascal's constants

synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: precipitate filtered, washed with methanol, dried in vacuum; dissolved in CHCl3/CH3OH (1:10), filtered; cubic crystals after 10 days

properties.summary: Powder of 2 shows very strong red Eu3+ luminescence at room temperature from 5D0→7FJ (J = 0–4), with the main emission 5D0→7F2. 5D0→7F0 and 5D0→7F1 are 60 and 10 times less intense, respectively; a singlet 5D0→7F0 near 578 nm indicates one emitting Eu1 site of C2v symmetry. Magnetically, μeff decreases continuously on cooling, consistent with single-ion Eu3+ behavior.

measurements.name: emission (5D0→7FJ)
measurements.conditions: solid powder, room temperature, λex = 465 nm; Hitachi F-4500

source_locations.location: Luminescence Spectroscopy of 2; Figure 4; Magnetic Properties

properties.summary: χM−1 vs T of 3 obeys Curie–Weiss law. Room-temperature μeff is close to nine noninteracting Gd3+ ions; μeff decreases gradually to 22.8 μB at 50 K then rapidly to 15.2 μB at 2 K, attributed mainly to weak intra- and intermolecular antiferromagnetic Gd3+ coupling, with possible zero-field splitting of 8S7/2.

measurements.conditions: Curie–Weiss fit of χM−1 vs T

measurements.name: μeff
measurements.conditions: 300 K / room temperature; calculated 23.8 μB for nine free Gd3+
